svg.text: Base class, function interfaces, five universal classes and derived types
physicalRef (points to a Device or Component — whichever is actually shared)
* VFD / Servo Drive appears under both classes — one physical device, always Controlling + Converting at once, optionally Transducer too
Peers of Device & Component — Added by Later Sub-models
same base class, same rules — none of these needed a new class tree of their own

most peers follow the pattern set by Interlock (Sub-model 6): their own id, own state, and a reference back to the object they concern — Operator is the exception, minimal by design (Sub-model 1 §5.2)

PredictedEvent.state: Open|Confirmed|Dismissed|Expired · ImprovementRecommendation.state: Proposed|UnderReview|Approved|Rejected|Applied · ChangeRequest/SecurityIncident: own lifecycles (Sub-model 13/10)
physicalRef — One Physical Asset, Many Functional Roles
optional on Device — targets whichever unit is actually shared: the Device itself, or one Component inside it
cf. OOP: the Proxy / Flyweight pattern — several instances, each with their own identity, sharing one implementation
single-CPU rack → physicalRef targets the Device itself, one shared asset for every role
omitted → the instance is assumed to be its own unique physical device
multi-CPU rack → physicalRef targets the specific Processor Component: two loops share CPU-A (patching it affects both together), one runs on independent CPU-B
each Processor Component still has its own id (Sub-model 1) — “not independently addressable” means not reachable directly on the network, not “without identity”
when every role in one Assembly's chain (S→T→CU→SC→A) shares the same physicalRef, that IS what “Integrated” means — now checkable, not just assumed
